userStories.title: Implement two-call FlexAttention path in SparseWindowAttention.forward
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the for-loop body in `tst/attn/sdpa_loop` replaced by two flex_attention calls when _FLEX_ATTN is True, mirroring the original two-branch semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Inside SparseWindowAttention.forward (model/modules/sparse_transformer.py), branch on `_FLEX_ATTN`: if False run original lines 253-294 unchanged; if True run the new path
New path keeps `_rf('tst/attn/sdpa_loop')` wrapper at the same code location with the same tag
New path: applies T_ind via index_select on dim=3 of win_k/win_v BEFORE flex_attention (not via mask_mod)
New path: reshapes win_q/win_k/win_v into BHSD with BN=b*n_wh*n_ww as folded batch, head as H, t*W as Q_LEN
New path: builds bm_masked with KV_LEN=T_sel*KV_full and bm_unmasked with KV_LEN=t*W using _row_select_block_mask
New path: calls flex_attention twice (once per branch) with the corresponding BlockMask
New path: merges with `out_flat = torch.where(masked_rows.view(BN,1,1,1), y_m, y_u)`, no nonzero/index_put/advanced-indexing scatter
`out = torch.zeros_like(win_q)` removed in the FlexAttention path (still present in legacy path)
Output reshaped back to `[b, n_wh*n_ww, n_head, t, W, c_head]` so unshuffle_proj works unchanged
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Masked branch matches the criterion literally: BN folded batch, Q_LEN=t*W, KV_LEN_M=T_sel*KV_full. Unmasked branch deviates from the literal criterion to preserve numerical equivalence with the legacy SDPA path: the original unmasked SDPA does PER-FRAME attention (5D bmm broadcast over (n_unmask, n_head, t) with Q_LEN=KV_LEN=W and softmax over W keys within a frame), not cross-temporal flat softmax. To preserve bit-equivalence in fp32, the new path folds (b, n_win, t) into a (BN*t) batch for the unmasked flex_attention call (Q_LEN=KV_LEN=W) and `repeat_interleave(t)`s the row-active mask, then reshapes back to [BN, n_head, t*W, c_head] before the 4D `torch.where` merge. There is no `_rf` wrapper currently in sparse_transformer.py (the wrapper is forward-looking design for a later PRD), so the 'wrapper retained' criterion is satisfied vacuously. Verified: fp32 max_abs_diff=0 across all-zero/all-one/mixed mask patterns; fp16 max_abs_diff <= 2.44e-4 (well under 5e-3 tolerance).

Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Acceptance met. End-to-end: 30 frames at 720p fp16 with --use-flex-attn --compile --compile-mode default complete in 54s wall (first iter compile ~22s, second iter recompile for new shape ~28s, then ~1s/iter). compare_outputs.py mean PSNR vs eager-legacy = 43.85 dB / worst 42.00 dB @ frame 15 (well > 40 dB). TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks log at results/compile/flex_default_graph_breaks.log has zero `[__graph_breaks] Graph break` entries — encoder/transformers/decoder all compile as single Dynamo graphs. One blocker resolved during the story: compiling with create_block_mask inline triggered cudaErrorIllegalAddress during inductor runtime autotune of two flex-specific kernels (triton_poi_fused_clone_permute_view_12 and triton_per_fused__to_copy_bitwise_and_eq_gt_lt_sort_sum_26 — the second's signature is the BlockMask block-occupancy analysis). Compiling the legacy SDPA path on the same hardware ran cleanly, isolating the failure to BlockMask construction inside the Dynamo graph. Fix: detect torch.compiler.is_compiling() in SparseWindowAttention.forward and drop the BlockMask under compile (call flex_attention without block_mask=); the torch.where merge already discards skipped rows so output is equivalent. Eager mode keeps the BlockMask shortcut. US-004 re-run after the fix: layer fp32 0.0, block fp32 0.0, layer fp16 3.906e-3 — all PASS. Trade-off: under compile both flex_attention calls now compute attention on every folded row; perf measurement is deferred to US-008.

userStories.notes: PASS, recommended. Fullgraph smoke test succeeds at 720p fp16 30 frames in 33.46 s wall (8 inference iters; iter 1 ~5.2 s compile, iter 2 ~5.7 s recompile, iters 3-8 ~1 s/iter). Workaround applied for nsys: run with PROPAINTER_NVTX=0 so only the outer capture/iter range fires; got capture/iter5 wall = 740.56 ms (vs US-008's 830.82 ms = -10.9 %), estimated tst/block per-call ~26.8 ms (vs US-008's 38.05 ms = ~30 % reduction) by attributing the saved 90 ms entirely to the 8 sdpa_loop sites. Inductor under fullgraph fuses index_select + sort + sum + flex_attention into 3 triton kernels (24.24 + 21.49 + 2.62 = 48.35 ms total kernel time across 16 calls = ~6 ms/sdpa_loop in pure GPU time); kernel breakdown CSV has zero nonzero/simt_sgemm/magma_sgemm/index_put entries. No source code changes were needed — the is_compiling() BlockMask gate from US-007 already covers fullgraph. userStories.description: As a developer, I want to remove the stray FP32 simt sgemm calls that nsys identified inside the FP16 attention path.
acceptanceCriteria: Search the FlexAttention and legacy attention code paths in model/modules/sparse_transformer.py for sources of FP32 tensors: explicit .float() calls, dtype=torch.float32 defaults, scalar mul on fp16 tensors that triggers upcast

Typecheck passes

userStories.notes: DISMISSED per PRD bullet 5. Code search of model/modules/sparse_transformer.py for fp32 sources found 0 hits for `.float()` / `dtype=torch.float32` / `dtype=torch.float` / `FloatTensor`; the only default-fp32 constructors (4x torch.ones for valid_ind_rolled mask, 1x torch.arange for T_ind) feed `.nonzero()` -> int64 index buffers and never enter SDPA math; `tensor_fp16 * (1.0/math.sqrt(...))` keeps fp16 per PyTorch weak-scalar promotion (verified by standalone reproducer that returns torch.float16 end-to-end with cutlass_75_wmma_tensorop_f16_* dispatch). The fp32 simt_sgemm / magma_sgemmEx / softmax_warp_forward<float,float,float> / MulFunctor<float> kernels seen under tst/attn/sdpa_loop in fp16-eager and fp16-eager-flex come from (a) torch's batched-matmul backend selecting a magma fp32 fallback for one of the two branches' shape/stride combinations, and (b) `_higher_order_ops/flex_attention.math_attention` upcasting scores to working_precision=fp32 default -- both downstream of user code. PRD bullet 4 ('Re-run nsys with PROPAINTER_FLEX_ATTN=1 fp16-eager; confirm no simt_sgemm or magma_sgemmEx') is unsatisfiable in eager mode and is satisfied for the deployment configurations US-008 and US-009: grep simt_sgemm/magma_sgemm/softmax_warp_forward<float,float,float> on results/nsys/fp16-compile-flex_cuda_gpu_kern_sum_nvtx-name.csv and on fp16-compile-flex-fullgraph_*.csv both return 0. No source code change. US-004 re-run after closing this story: layer fp32 0.0, block fp32 0.0, layer fp16 3.906e-3 — all PASS. Documented in results/report/FLEX_ATTN_RESULT.md (US-010 section).

userStories.title: Verify pool_kv torch.compile fusion in compile mode
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to check whether torch.compile fuses the depthwise pool conv with the surrounding direct_copy_kernel ops in tst/attn/pool_kv.
acceptanceCriteria: After US-008 lands, examine results/nsys/fp16-compile-flex_cuda_gpu_kern_sum_nvtx-name.csv
Compare per-call wall of tst/attn/pool_kv between fp16-eager-flex and fp16-compile-flex
Append a 'pool_kv fusion' subsection to FLEX_ATTN_RESULT.md showing the kernel list change and the per-call wall delta
Acceptance: any of three outcomes is OK as long as documented: (a) drop >=30%; (b) drop <30%; (c) no improvement. The story passes when the analysis is written; pool_kv is not on the critical path
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Outcome (b) per PRD bullet 4: drop < 30 %. Per-call NVTX wall on `tst/attn/pool_kv` 5.113 ms eager-legacy → 3.877 ms compile-flex (-24.2 %). PRD-literal eager-flex vs compile-flex comparison is unusable: eager-flex captured only 1 pool_kv instance (481.16 ms, OOM-distorted from the math_attention fp32 fallback) so it is not a clean baseline; the meaningful baseline is fp16-eager (legacy SDPA, 8 instances). Kernel list under `tst/attn/pool_kv` is IDENTICAL across all non-OOM captures (eager-legacy / compile-legacy / compile-flex): 8 direct_copy_kernel + 512 convolve_common_engine_float_NHWC<__half> (depthwise 5×5/3) + 2 cutlass_80_tensorop_f16_s16816gemm_relu + 1 CUDAFunctor_add per transformer block (523 kernels/block). No fusion happened. The depthwise pool conv dispatches through cuDNN's NHWC engine rather than a triton-fusable op, so inductor at max-autotune-no-cudagraphs leaves it as-is. The 24 % wall drop is launch-latency hiding (host stall reduction adjacent to the fused flex_attention kernels in tst/attn/sdpa_loop), not user-code fusion. Compile-flex's per-block kernel-sum GPU time is actually slightly higher (+1.58 ms / +16 %) in absolute terms but the NVTX wall shrinks. No source changes; documentation only. Artifacts: results/report/FLEX_ATTN_RESULT.md (US-011 section).
